newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Alatas hopes to see Cambodian premiers.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Alatas hopes to see Cambodian premiers.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Wednesday he might have separate meetings with Cambodia's warring prime ministers after talks with King Sihanouk in Beijing on Thursday.
Alatas was leaving Jakarta on Wednesday on a special plane to Beijing, where he was joining the foreign ministers of Thailand and the Philippines for the meeting with Sihanouk.

The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) decided last week to postpone Cambodia's accession to the seven-nation organisation following the ousting of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, Sihanouk's son, by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

Alatas said he might meet Ranariddh in Bangkok on Friday and then hoped to go to Phnom Penh as soon as possible for talks with Hun Sen. Last week's ASEAN session mandated Alatas, Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn and Philippines Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon to meet Sihanouk. Alatas did not say if all three would also meet the two Cambodian premiers.

Alatas told reporters after meeting Indonesian President Suharto on Wednesday that the ASEAN ministers would convey the decision to postpone Cambodia's entry to Sihanouk and listen to his views on the situation in Cambodia. Sihanouk on Tuesday accused the police and army of Hun Sen of torturing and killing political opponents and urged an end to the bloodshed in Cambodia. "We will listen to Sihanouk's views and suggestions on how we can help to find solutions if all parties in the dispute are willing," Alatas said before leaving for the flight to Beijing.
"We don't have any recipe to solve the problem...so we will listen to his views," Alatas added.

He denied accusations by Hun Sen that ASEAN was interfering in Cambodia's internal affairs, and he declined to comment on a statement by the premier that he might withdraw Cambodia's application to join ASEAN.

ASEAN currently comprises Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam and Brunei. Cambodia had been due to join ASEAN together with Burma and Laos at a 30th anniversary meeting in Kuala Lumpur late this month.
